subject: Retail partner surge -> intermittent parse errors in client SDK (urgent escalation)
messages:
From: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@clearretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@clearretail.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: spikes + parse failures during midday surge

Hi Evelyn,

We started seeing an uptick in 5xxs around 11:30AM PT when traffic spiked ~3x. Errors look like streaming parse failures on the client SDK side: the gateway logs show repeated "invalid header boundary" and some of our ingesters are dropping the connection mid-stream. Attached is a log snippet and a screenshot of p99 latency for the hour.

Impact: intermittent checkout failures (~2.3% error rate) and higher token costs due to retries. This is customer-facing for ClearRetail's flash sale so it's high priority for them.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is an SDK regression or something on our side? We rolled the latest SDK patch earlier this week (v2.1.8).

Thanks,
Clara
Clara Nguyen
Head of Integrations, ClearRetail

Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: spikes + parse failures during midday surge

Folks — preliminary findings after looking at the provided logs and in-cluster captures:

- ClearRetail traffic pattern shows many large initial headers (custom metadata) that exceed our streaming parser's fast-path assumption when the client batches many events per connection. The parser's header reassembly logic assumes headers arrive in <= 8KB segments; we've observed split boundaries at ~12-14KB which triggers an out-of-path code path that hasn't been exercised in recent CI.
- Under high concurrency we see a race between the header-append buffer and the parser state machine resulting in intermittent "invalid header boundary" and then a connection abort.
- This is reproducible with a local harness simulating their header sizes + 3x concurrency.

Action items:
1) Karthik: prepare a runtime hotfix to make the header reassembly tolerant to larger chunk splits and add defensive checks. Try to get a gated build by EOD.
2) Marissa/SE: coordinate a short client-side mitigation we can advise ClearRetail to apply (reduce per-connection batch size / set max-chunk-size to 8KB) while we push the fix.
3) Evelyn: please gather the SDK exact sha and any proxy/load-balancer settings they use.

I'll keep digging into memory ordering blame but this looks like a parser edge-case that regressed after the refactor we shipped last quarter.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: ingest-sample-headers.txt (captured problematic header frames)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: spikes + parse failures during midday surge

Clara — thanks for the quick confirm; their SDK sha is v2.1.8 (build 20270401-8f2c3c). Their infra team also says they have an inline proxy that does header enrichment.

Suggested immediate mitigation for your ops team:
- Set client config max_batch_per_connection=50 (down from 200)
- Enable keepalive and set max_chunk_size=8192

Aditya has a reproduction. We'll push a runtime mitigation and aim for a patched build within the day. If this is disruptive to traffic we can open a short maintenance window to roll the fix.

We'll update you with a timeline in the next hour.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evan Timmons <evan_timmons@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Retail partner surge -> intermittent parse errors in client SDK (urgent escalation)

Forwarding triage summary for exec attention. (Forwarded message below)

Triage summary:
- Root cause: header reassembly race in streaming parser triggered by oversized header frames combined with high concurrency and certain proxy-enrichment behavior. Not an SDK wire protocol violation; it's a runtime parser robustness regression introduced during last quarter's parser refactor.
- Scope: ClearRetail observed ~2.3% checkout failures during a 90-minute window at peak; other customers with large metadata headers may be at risk under similar bursts. No data leakage.
- Immediate mitigations completed:
  * Deployed a patched parser build to the affected runtime pool at 16:30 PT (hotfix v1.0.13) with relaxed boundary checks and additional synchronization.
  * Recommended and verified client config changes for ClearRetail (max_chunk_size=8192, smaller per-connection batches).
  * Short-term gauge: error rate dropped from 2.3% -> 0.1% after mitigation.
- Next steps:
  * Postmortem (owner: Marissa) due Monday 2027-04-05.
  * Add regression tests to CI to cover split-header sizes and high-concurrency harness (owner: Karthik).
  * Outreach: Evelyn to coordinate customer communication and credit discussion if requested.

Requesting exec review: We propose an internal incident write-up and a targeted audit of parser changes from last quarter. If OK, please ACK and we'll publish the postmortem and customer-facing note.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
